title: Vegan Panna Cotta
subtitle: Coconut cream set with agar, infused with vanilla
excerpt: Coconut cream and oat milk set with agar into a smooth, firm dome. The texture is slightly more decisive than gelatine-set panna cotta, but the flavour is clean and unmistakably coconut-vanilla.
sourceNotes: A dairy-free, plant-based adaptation of the Italian panna cotta, using agar-agar, a seaweed-derived setting agent, in place of gelatine. Agar has been used in Asian cooking for centuries and became widely available in British home cooking in the early 21st century as plant-based cooking gained mainstream ground.

recipe.batchNotes: Can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept in the moulds in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before. Turn out just before serving.

content.text: Vegan panna cotta sets with agar-agar rather than gelatine. The result is slightly firmer and holds its shape more cleanly on the plate. Agar must come to a full boil to activate. That is the one step where this differs from the gelatine method.

items.prepNote: from a 400ml can, shake well before opening
powder or flakes, if using flakes, use 2 level teaspoons

content.text: Lightly oil 4 to 6 ramekins with a neutral oil. Pour the coconut cream and oat milk into a small saucepan and whisk together until smooth. Add the caster sugar and agar-agar powder, and whisk to combine. Place over a medium heat and bring to the boil, stirring constantly, the agar must reach a full boil to activate. Once boiling, reduce the heat and stir for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla bean paste.

Pour the mixture through a fine sieve into a jug, then divide between the prepared ramekins. Leave to cool to room temperature, agar begins setting at around 40°C, so the mixture will firm up faster than gelatine. Once cool, cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. To unmould, run a thin knife around the inside edge, place a plate over the top, and invert firmly.

items.cause: The agar did not reach a full boil, or the quantity was too low.
items.fix: Agar must boil to activate, a simmer is not sufficient. If the mixture has not set after 2 hours, return it to the saucepan, bring to the boil again with an extra 0.5 teaspoon of agar, then re-pour and chill.

items.cause: The agar was not fully dissolved before boiling, or flakes were used without soaking.
items.fix: Whisk the agar into the cold liquid before heating so it disperses evenly. If using flakes, soak in the cold liquid for 5 minutes first to help them dissolve.

items.cause: Full-fat coconut cream has a pronounced flavour that some find too strong.
items.fix: Replace 100ml of the coconut cream with additional oat milk, or add 1 teaspoon of lemon juice to the finished mixture to cut through the richness.

content.text: Keeps in the moulds in the fridge for up to 3 days. Agar-set desserts hold their structure well and do not weep as gelatine-set ones sometimes do. Do not freeze.
